name: Absorption (gold)
why: Sellers hit hard but price closes in the top half: a big passive buyer is soaking up the selling. When sellers run out, price lifts. Short = mirror.
data: Bybit gold tape, real buyer/seller side
note: Edge before fees ≈ 0 on 15m–1h; the fee takes 0.12–0.26R a trade. Order flow did not beat the same rule without it. 4h looked good on too few trades.

name: Absorption 4h on 5 markets
why: Same rule, unchanged, 4h only — more markets to reach 0.5 trades/day.
data: Bybit tapes (gold, PAXG gold token, silver); Binance taker volume (BTC, ETH)
luck: gold long p 0.02–0.03 vs same bars; 29 tests → expected by chance
note: BTC loses in every version, ETH ≈ 0, silver too few trades. Only gold LONG hints at something, but the stricter version is worse and the first half of 3 years made nothing. A note, not a strategy.

name: Fade the crowd (gold)
why: Bybit gold traders are small leveraged accounts. When they are unusually one-sided and piling in, a small move against them forces exits that push price further — we take the other side.
data: Bybit long/short account share + open interest, hourly (used 1h late)
note: Edge before fees ≈ 0 on the 3-year market in every version. The crowd is 51–75% long at all times and grew with the gold rally — knowing it tells nothing about the next 1–48h.

name: Opening range breakout (simple)
why: The session open is where the day's orders arrive; the first break out of the opening range is the side that won the open and should run into the close.
note: 0 of 60 make money at 2x fees. There IS a small edge before fees — 39 of 60 versions positive, best +0.10R a trade (gold London 15m, 30-min range, hold to close) — but the range stop is tight, so fees take 0.08–0.16R a trade and wipe it out. NAS100 NY 5m/15m picks direction better than a coin (p 0.015) and still loses.

name: ORB as actually traded (research)
why: Rebuilt from research: Zarattini & Aziz first-5m-candle ORB (10R or close), prop-firm NQ 15m range / measured-move target, gold ORB script (mid stop, 2x target), entries only in the first 2.5h, plus the 'in-play' filter (opening volume ≥ 1.5x its 14-day average).
pf2x: 0.52–0.99 without filter · in-play up to 1.68 on 14 trades
note: Reproduces the paper's finding: NAS100 NY first-candle ORB makes +0.07R before fees (paper +0.13R), and fees take 0.09R. The 15m range versions on NAS100 NY are +0.05R before fees and PF 1.03 at 1x — break-even. The in-play filter roughly triples the edge before fees (gold London +0.36R, NAS100 London +0.34R) but leaves 14–106 trades and does not beat the luck check across 28 versions.

name: Kris's ORB: first candle, break, retest
why: Kris's own rules: wait for the first 5m/15m candle of London or NY, a later candle closes beyond it, enter on the retest of the broken level.
note: Win rate 27–53% with targets of 1–2R. A 70% win rate needs a target of about 0.4R, and there it loses: NAS100 NY 15m at 0.5R target wins 67% and makes −0.025R a trade after normal fees; at 0.25R it wins 76% and makes −0.075R. Best version (NAS100 NY 15m, stop other side, 1R) is break-even before the 2x fee. Retest fills are assumed on a touch, which flatters it.

name: Trend following swing: 1 entry, 6 exits
why: Trends last longer than random because news and positioning arrive slowly. A trend follower loses small and often and lives on a few long runs, so the exit decides whether those runs are kept.
data: Dukascopy 5-year 4h (gold, silver, EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY), Binance BTC, NAS100 3 years
pf2x: 4h books 1.02–1.13 · daily books 1.04–1.28 · gold daily 1.45–2.36 (39–58 trades) · BTC 4h 1.10–1.52
days: 4h book 15–25 d (32–36% pass, 2.8–3.2 accounts) · daily 65–117 d
luck: 12 of 84 cells beat random entries at p<0.05 vs 4 expected
verdict: WEAK — real but too slow / too thin
note: Real trend effect: 12 of 84 market×exit cells beat random entries (4 expected). But the MARKET decides far more than the exit: gold, BTC and USDJPY win with every exit, EURUSD and GBPUSD lose with every exit, and no exit makes random entries profitable. Among exits, 'let it run' (break-even + trail, ATR trail, turtle) beats time exits on both timeframes; the 20-bar time exit is worst. Picking markets on the first half did not reliably help the second half on 4h.
